title: Machine end
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/dispatches/<dispatch_id>/machine-end, application/json: the starter reports the result of deleting the machine it created for the dispatch. The starter sends the call for a machine it created for the dispatch, and for no other machine. A dispatch for which it made no machine, or whose machine id it never learned, gets no call. The starter sends the call after its delete call, the command delete of the machine adapter, https://qory.dev/contracts/machines/v1/delete.schema.json. It repeats the delete call until that call returns gone, and then sends gone. The call may come any number of times, before or after the dispatch ends. Each send is built anew, with a later time and a new signature, as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes for a request sent again, so the replay rule does not refuse it. The starter sends one call at a time for a dispatch: it sends the next only after the answer to the one before, or after it gave that one up. The control plane applies the calls in the order it receives them and compares no time, and every accepted call replaces the state, so delete_failed can be followed by deleting. The state gone is final: a later call changes nothing and still gets the 204. The call is optional for a starter: a starter that never sends it still works. A dispatch_id that is unknown, or of another node pool than the key's, is refused 403 forbidden, with the same signed body either way, so nobody learns whether an id exists. The signature with the pool's access key and that check authorise the request, not the id. A signed 403 or 404 ends the starter's attempts to send this call for the dispatch; the delete calls go on. After any other failure, an unsigned answer among them, the starter sends the call again for a limited time and then drops it, because the call is optional. The starter counts a machine against its limit of machines only until the delete call returns gone, whatever the answers to this call, so a control plane without the route blocks no machine. A machine end is refused for the first of these that applies, in this order: 403 forbidden, as above; 503 unavailable, the control plane cannot store the call at that moment, and the starter sends it again later, built anew. It is never refused 410 gone or 409 lease_expired, because a machine usually ends after its dispatch. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. The request is signed with the pool's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the starter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

state.description: The result of deleting the machine. deleting: the starter's delete call was accepted, and the machine may still exist. gone: the machine adapter's delete call returned that no machine with the id exists at the vendor, https://qory.dev/contracts/machines/v1/delete-answer.schema.json. A missing entry in a list is no proof, because a vendor's list can lag. delete_failed: the delete call failed, and as far as the starter knows the machine still exists.
